background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: You have a budget-balanced legislation or a piece of budget-balanced legislation in the works. Explain what that is and how it's different not only from what the Democrats are proposing but from what other Republicans have proposed.

ground_truth: Well, what it does is it balances current spending with the average revenues of the previous three years. And that has a lot of nice effects that people in both parties like. If you are looking at it from the case where you don't want government spending to be suddenly cut during a recession, well, this balanced budget amendment allows you to keep spending at the level of the previous three years of revenue. So if you have a sudden recession, your tax revenues are low, you don't have to suddenly slash government programs. You can do it in a more calculated way. You can think about the long run. And if you are worried about tax increases, well, I think it's got a good defense against tax increases because you have to make the case that you want to increase taxes for the long run under my proposal because any tax increases that are incurred in the current year can't be used for current year spending.
